title: Tracing every path
idea: A nested if has several paths. Tracing each one by hand builds confidence that you know exactly which branch runs. Predict output for all cases.

exercises.prompt: Count the paths. This nested if has an outer if/else and an inner if/else inside the outer if. How many possible printed results?
exercises.explanation: Outer-False gives one result. Outer-True then splits into inner-True and inner-False. That is 1 + 2 = 3 paths.
30 >= 25 is True, so we enter; sunny is True, so 'Beach day'.

exercises.prompt: Same code, temp = 30, sunny = False. What prints?
exercises.explanation: Still warm (30 >= 25), but sunny is False, so the inner else runs: 'Warm but grey'.

exercises.prompt: Same code, temp = 10, sunny = True. What prints?
exercises.explanation: 10 >= 25 is False, so the outer else runs: 'Too cold'. The sunny check is skipped because we never entered the outer body.

exercises.prompt: Match each (temp, sunny) case to its output for the beach code.
exercises.explanation: When temp is below 25, 'sunny' never gets checked - the outer gate decides first.

exercises.prompt: When temp is 10, the value of 'sunny' makes no difference to the output.
exercises.explanation: Correct. A False outer condition skips the whole body, so the inner check on 'sunny' never runs.
100 >= 40 so funds are fine; then 40 >= 50 is False, so the inner else: 'Normal withdrawal'.

exercises.prompt: Same code, balance = 30, withdraw = 40. What prints?
exercises.explanation: 30 >= 40 is False, so we go straight to the outer else: 'Insufficient funds'. The size check never happens.

exercises.prompt: Put the tracing steps in the order a careful reader uses.
blocks: If outer is False, run the outer else and stop
If outer is True, check the inner condition
Run the inner branch that matches
exercises.explanation: Outer first, then inner only if you got inside. Tracing in this order never misleads you.

exercises.prompt: Why trace every path before trusting a nested if?
options: To be sure each real-life case lands in the branch you intended
There is no reason to trace
exercises.explanation: Tracing each case proves your branches match the rules. A missed path is the classic nested-if bug.
